source.text: Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐλεύθερος;

records.literal_gloss: Not am I free?

en.L: Am I not free?
en.B: Am I not free?
en.R: Am I not free?

fr.L: Ne suis-je pas libre ?
fr.B: Ne suis-je pas libre ?
fr.R: Ne suis-je pas libre ?

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes: Paul is free
alternatives: a real question about whether he is free
decisions.reason: Οὐκ in a question looks for the answer yes. The four questions of verse 1 are Paul's own claims, put as questions the Corinthians cannot deny.

decisions.choice: free: under no one's control, with every right to act as he chooses
decisions.reason: The word picks up the "right" (freedom) of the strong in 8:9. Chapter 9 makes Paul an example: he has rights, as an apostle, and gives them up for others, as he asked the strong to do in chapter 8. In 9:19 he says it again: free from all, he made himself a slave to all.

source.text: οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος;

records.literal_gloss: Not am I an apostle?

en.L: Am I not an apostle?
en.B: Am I not an apostle?
en.R: Am I not an apostle?

fr.L: Ne suis-je pas apôtre ?
fr.B: Ne suis-je pas apôtre ?
fr.R: Ne suis-je pas apôtre ?

decisions.choice: apostle: one sent out by the risen Lord with his authority, to found and lead churches
decisions.reason: ἀπόστολος means someone sent. For Paul it names those whom Christ himself commissioned (1:1; 15:7-9; Galatians 1:1). Some in Corinth questioned whether he had this standing (verse 3; 2 Corinthians 10-13), so verses 1-2 defend it before he speaks of an apostle's rights.

source.text: οὐχὶ Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἑόρακα;

records.literal_gloss: Not Jesus the Lord of us have I seen?

en.L: Have I not seen Jesus our Lord?
en.B: Have I not seen Jesus our Lord?
en.R: Did I not see Jesus our Lord for myself?

fr.L: N’ai-je pas vu Jésus notre Seigneur ?
fr.B: N’ai-je pas vu Jésus notre Seigneur ?
fr.R: N’ai-je pas vu moi-même Jésus notre Seigneur ?

decisions.choice: seen Jesus our Lord: seen the risen Lord, who appeared to Paul and called him
alternatives: a vision of the kind any believer might have
decisions.reason: Paul lists himself among those to whom the risen Christ appeared (15:8), on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:3-6; Galatians 1:15-16). Having seen the risen Lord was part of what made an apostle (Acts 1:21-22), so this question supports the one before it.

decisions.choice: a question that strongly expects yes; the perfect tense describes a seeing whose effect lasts
decisions.reason: οὐχὶ is a stronger form of the negative and asks for a firm yes. The perfect ἑόρακα points to a past event that still stands as Paul's credential.

decisions.choice: for myself (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "for myself" to show that Paul is speaking of a personal meeting with the risen Lord (m1), which is the point of the question.

source.text: οὐ τὸ ἔργον μου ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν κυρίῳ;

records.literal_gloss: Not the work of me you are in [the] Lord?

en.L: Are you not my work in [the] Lord?
en.B: Are you not what my work in the Lord has produced?
en.R: Are you not the result of the work I did for the Lord?

fr.L: N’êtes-vous pas mon œuvre dans le Seigneur ?
fr.B: N’êtes-vous pas le fruit de mon travail dans le Seigneur ?
fr.R: N’êtes-vous pas le résultat du travail que j’ai fait pour le Seigneur ?

decisions.choice: my work: what Paul's labor produced, the church that came to be through his preaching
decisions.reason: Paul planted the church in Corinth (3:6, 10; 4:15; Acts 18:1-11). The Corinthians themselves are the work: their faith is the visible result of his apostleship, as verse 2 goes on to say.

decisions.choice: in the Lord: the work was done in union with the Lord and by his power, and the Corinthians are in the Lord
alternatives: only a description of where they now are
decisions.reason: The phrase qualifies the claim. They are Paul's work only because the Lord worked through him (3:5-7), and their life as believers is lived in the Lord.

decisions.choice: what my work ... has produced (B); the result of the work I did for the Lord (R)
decisions.reason: "You are my work" is not natural English for people. Balanced and Readable say that they are what Paul's work produced (m1).

source.text: εἰ ἄλλοις οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος, ἀλλά γε ὑμῖν εἰμι, ἡ γὰρ σφραγίς μου τῆς ἀποστολῆς ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν κυρίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: If to others not I am an apostle, yet at least to you I am; the for seal of me of the apostleship you are in [the] Lord.

en.L: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least to you I am; for you are the seal of my apostleship in [the] Lord.
en.B: Others may not count me as an apostle, but to you I certainly am one. For you yourselves, in the Lord, are the seal that proves my apostleship.
en.R: Other people may not accept me as an apostle, but you surely must. You belong to the Lord because of my work, and that proves that I am an apostle.

fr.L: Si pour d’autres je ne suis pas apôtre, pour vous du moins je le suis ; car le sceau de mon apostolat, c’est vous, dans le Seigneur.
fr.B: D’autres ne me considèrent peut-être pas comme un apôtre, mais pour vous je le suis certainement. Car c’est vous-mêmes, dans le Seigneur, qui êtes le sceau qui authentifie mon apostolat.
fr.R: D’autres refusent peut-être de me reconnaître comme apôtre, mais vous, vous devez le faire. Vous appartenez au Seigneur grâce à mon travail, et cela prouve que je suis apôtre.

decisions.choice: to others ... to you: in the view of others ... in your view
alternatives: for others (churches Paul did not found) ... for you
decisions.reason: The datives can mean "in the opinion of" or "for the benefit of". The contrast with "you" and the defense that follows (verse 3) suggest that some people, perhaps outsiders, did not recognize Paul. Even if they doubt him, the Corinthians of all people cannot. ἀλλά γε means "yet at least".

decisions.choice: seal: a mark pressed in wax with a signet, which showed that a document or goods were genuine and authorized
decisions.reason: A seal confirmed that something was what it claimed to be. A church brought into being through Paul's preaching is God's own confirmation of his apostleship (compare 2 Corinthians 3:2-3).

decisions.choice: apostleship: the commission and work of an apostle
decisions.reason: ἀποστολή names the office of an apostle (Romans 1:5; Galatians 2:8).

decisions.choice: You belong to the Lord because of my work (R)
alternatives: you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable explains the seal picture: their being in the Lord through Paul's work is the proof (m2).

source.text: Ἡ ἐμὴ ἀπολογία τοῖς ἐμὲ ἀνακρίνουσίν ἐστιν αὕτη.

records.literal_gloss: The my defense to those me examining is this.

en.L: My defense to those who examine me is this:
en.B: This is my defense to those who put me on trial:
en.R: Some people want to put me on trial. Here is how I answer them.

fr.L: Ma défense devant ceux qui m’examinent, la voici :
fr.B: Voici ma défense devant ceux qui me font un procès :
fr.R: Certains veulent me faire un procès. Voici ce que je leur réponds.

decisions.choice: defense ... examine: courtroom words for a reply to a charge and for questioning someone under trial
alternatives: a calm explanation to friendly questioners
decisions.reason: ἀπολογία is the answer an accused person gives in court; ἀνακρίνω is the verb Paul used in 2:14-15 and 4:3-4, where he refuses to be judged by any human court. Some in Corinth were sitting in judgment on him.

decisions.choice: this: points forward to the argument of verses 4-23
decisions.reason: αὕτη stands last for emphasis. It can sum up the questions of verses 1-2 (the Corinthians themselves are his proof) or introduce what follows. The questions that follow (verses 4-6) are the start of the reply to his critics, which explains why he does not take support.

decisions.choice: examine (L); put me on trial (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the courtroom picture (m1), as in 4:3-4.

source.text: μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν φαγεῖν καὶ πεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Not not have we [the] right to eat and to drink?

en.L: Do we not have [the] right to eat and drink?
en.B: Surely we have the right to be given food and drink?
en.R: Surely we have the right to be given food and drink by those we serve.

fr.L: N’avons-nous pas le droit de manger et de boire ?
fr.B: Nous avons bien le droit de recevoir à manger et à boire, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Nous avons bien le droit de recevoir à manger et à boire de ceux que nous servons.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes: surely we have that right
decisions.reason: μὴ οὐκ puts a question marker before a negative: "It is not that we do not have ..., is it?" The double negative asks the readers to agree.

decisions.choice: the right to eat and drink: the right to receive food and drink from the churches, at their expense
alternatives: the right to eat any food, including food offered to idols
decisions.reason: ἐξουσίαν is the "right" of 8:9, but the following verses (6-14) are about apostles being supported by those they serve, so eating and drinking here means being fed by the church.

decisions.choice: we: Paul and his co-workers, Barnabas especially (verse 6)
alternatives: Paul alone, speaking of himself as "we"
decisions.reason: Verse 6 names Barnabas with Paul, and both had refused support. In verse 15 Paul turns to "I".

decisions.choice: to be given food and drink (B); by those we serve (R)
decisions.reason: "The right to eat and drink" would sound like the freedom to eat anything. Balanced and Readable say what is meant (m2).

source.text: μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν ἀδελφὴν γυναῖκα περιάγειν, ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ Κηφᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: Not not have we [the] right a sister [as] wife to take along, as also the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?

en.L: Do we not have [the] right to take along a sister [as] a wife, as also the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas [do]?
en.B: Surely we have the right to take a believing wife with us on our travels, as the other apostles do, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
en.R: Surely we have the right to bring a believing wife with us when we travel. The other apostles do that, and so do the Lord's brothers and Peter.

fr.L: N’avons-nous pas le droit d’emmener avec nous une sœur [comme] épouse, comme aussi les autres apôtres et les frères du Seigneur et Céphas ?
fr.B: N’avons-nous pas le droit d’emmener dans nos voyages une épouse croyante, comme le font les autres apôtres, les frères du Seigneur et Céphas ?
fr.R: Nous avons bien le droit d’emmener avec nous une épouse croyante quand nous voyageons. C’est ce que font les autres apôtres, les frères du Seigneur et Pierre.

decisions.choice: a sister as wife: a wife who is a fellow believer
alternatives: a Christian woman who is not a wife, traveling as a helper
decisions.reason: ἀδελφὴν is the usual word for a fellow believer who is a woman (7:15; Romans 16:1), and γυναῖκα here means wife, as in 7:2-4. The point is that apostles may marry and have their wives travel with them, supported by the churches.

decisions.choice: the brothers of the Lord: the brothers of Jesus named in the Gospels, who came to believe after his resurrection
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names James, Joses, Judas and Simon. They did not believe in him during his ministry (John 7:5) but are with the disciples after the resurrection (Acts 1:14), and James became a leader of the Jerusalem church (15:7; Galatians 1:19). Christian traditions differ on whether they were sons of Mary and Joseph, sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage, or cousins; ἀδελφοὶ normally means brothers.

decisions.choice: Cephas: Peter, called by his Aramaic name; he was married
decisions.reason: Jesus healed Peter's mother-in-law (Mark 1:30). Naming him last gives weight to the example: even the leading apostle took his wife along.

decisions.choice: [as] a wife (L); believing wife (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Sister" in this sense is church language; Balanced and Readable say plainly that she is a believer (m1). Literal keeps "sister" so the form can be seen.

decisions.choice: Peter (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:12 and 3:22, Readable uses the name readers know.

source.text: ἢ μόνος ἐγὼ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν μὴ ἐργάζεσθαι;

records.literal_gloss: Or only I and Barnabas not have we [the] right not to work?

en.L: Or [is it] only I and Barnabas [who] do not have [the] right not to work?
en.B: Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to stop working for a living?
en.R: Or do only Barnabas and I have no right to give up working to earn our own living?

fr.L: Ou bien moi seul et Barnabas, n’avons-nous pas le droit de ne pas travailler ?
fr.B: Ou bien sommes-nous les seuls, Barnabas et moi, à ne pas avoir le droit de cesser de travailler pour gagner notre vie ?
fr.R: Ou alors, Barnabas et moi, est-ce que nous serions les seuls à ne pas avoir le droit d’être nourris sans devoir gagner notre vie ?

decisions.choice: Barnabas: Paul's early partner in mission, who also supported himself
decisions.reason: Barnabas brought Paul to the church leaders in Jerusalem and to Antioch and traveled with him (Acts 9:27; 11:25-26; 13-14). This verse shows that he, like Paul, worked with his hands rather than accept support.

decisions.choice: not to work: to be free from earning a living by a trade, because the church provides support
decisions.reason: Paul worked as a tentmaker or leatherworker (Acts 18:3; 1 Corinthians 4:12; 1 Thessalonians 2:9). To "not work" means to live on the support of those one serves, as verses 7-14 argue.

decisions.choice: Barnabas and I (B, R)
decisions.reason: English puts "I" last in such pairs. Literal keeps the Greek order.

source.text: τίς στρατεύεται ἰδίοις ὀψωνίοις ποτέ;

records.literal_gloss: Who serves as a soldier at own wages ever?

en.L: Who ever serves as a soldier at [his] own expense?
en.B: Who ever serves in an army and pays his own costs?
en.R: Does a soldier ever have to pay his own way?

fr.L: Qui sert jamais comme soldat à ses propres frais ?
fr.B: Qui part jamais à l’armée en payant lui-même ses dépenses ?
fr.R: Est-ce qu’un soldat doit payer lui-même ce dont il a besoin ?

decisions.choice: own wages: the rations and pay a soldier received from whoever enlisted him
decisions.reason: ὀψώνιον was a soldier's ration money and pay (Luke 3:14). No one expected a soldier to fund his own service.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: The first of three everyday pictures (soldier, vine grower, shepherd) in which a worker lives from his work. Paul uses the same pictures of himself elsewhere: a soldier (2 Corinthians 10:3-4), a planter (3:6).

source.text: τίς φυτεύει ἀμπελῶνα καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐσθίει;

records.literal_gloss: Who plants a vineyard and the fruit of it not eats?

en.L: Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit?
en.B: Who plants a vineyard and eats none of its grapes?
en.R: Who plants a vineyard and then never eats any of the grapes?

fr.L: Qui plante une vigne et n’en mange pas le fruit ?
fr.B: Qui plante une vigne sans en manger le raisin ?
fr.R: Qui plante une vigne et ne mange jamais un seul de ses raisins ?

decisions.choice: the vine grower who eats the fruit: a picture also found in the Old Testament
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 20:6 and Proverbs 27:18 assume that the one who plants or tends a crop enjoys its fruit.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "eat its fruit"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "of its fruit", a small change of construction with the same meaning; the SBLGNT text, with the earlier manuscripts, has "its fruit". Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

source.text: τίς ποιμαίνει ποίμνην καὶ ἐκ τοῦ γάλακτος τῆς ποίμνης οὐκ ἐσθίει;

records.literal_gloss: Who shepherds a flock and from the milk of the flock not eats?

en.L: Who shepherds a flock and does not eat from the milk of the flock?
en.B: Who tends a flock and gets none of its milk?
en.R: Who takes care of a flock and never drinks any of its milk?

fr.L: Qui fait paître un troupeau et ne mange pas du lait du troupeau ?
fr.B: Qui garde un troupeau sans profiter de son lait ?
fr.R: Qui s’occupe d’un troupeau et ne boit jamais de son lait ?

decisions.choice: eat from the milk: live in part on the milk of the flock and what is made from it
decisions.reason: Greek uses "eat" here to match the line before; milk and cheese were part of a shepherd's daily food.

decisions.choice: eat (L); gets (B); drinks (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek verb; Balanced and Readable use a verb that suits milk (m1).

source.text: Μὴ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ταῦτα λαλῶ ἢ καὶ ὁ νόμος ταῦτα οὐ λέγει;

records.literal_gloss: Not according to man these things do I speak, or also the law these things not says?

en.L: Am I saying these things according to man? Or does the law not say these things too?
en.B: Am I saying this only on human authority? Does the law not say the same thing?
en.R: Is this just a human way of thinking? Does the law of Moses not say the same thing?

fr.L: Est-ce selon l’homme que je dis ces choses ? Ou bien la Loi ne dit-elle pas aussi ces choses ?
fr.B: Est-ce que je dis cela seulement d’après une autorité humaine ? La Loi ne dit-elle pas la même chose ?
fr.R: Est-ce seulement une façon humaine de voir les choses ? La Loi de Moïse ne dit-elle pas la même chose ?

decisions.choice: according to man: by ordinary human reasoning, from everyday examples only
decisions.reason: Paul uses the phrase for a merely human point of view (3:3; 15:32; Romans 3:5). The examples of verse 7 come from daily life; now he appeals to Scripture.

decisions.choice: two questions: the first expects no, the second expects yes
decisions.reason: Μὴ looks for the answer no, οὐ for yes: "I am not speaking only on human grounds, am I? Does the law not say the same?"

decisions.choice: the law: the Law of Moses, the first five books of Scripture
decisions.reason: Verse 9 names it "the law of Moses" and quotes Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the law, as verse 9 does (m3).

decisions.choice: la Loi, capitalised, for the Law of Moses (9:8-9, 20-21); lowercase for law in general ("sans loi", "la loi de Dieu", "la loi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", 9:21)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the whole New Testament, the capital marks the Law of Moses (m3). In verse 21 Paul speaks of being bound to God's law and to Christ's law, which are not the Law of Moses, so French writes them in lowercase and the contrast stays visible.

source.text: ἐν γὰρ τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ γέγραπται· Οὐ κημώσεις βοῦν ἀλοῶντα.

records.literal_gloss: In for the of Moses law it has been written: Not you shall muzzle an ox threshing.

en.L: For in the law of Moses it has been written, "You shall not muzzle an ox [that is] threshing."
en.B: For in the law of Moses it is written, "Do not muzzle an ox that is threshing grain."
en.R: The law of Moses says, "When an ox is threshing grain, do not put a muzzle on its mouth."

fr.L: Car dans la Loi de Moïse il a été écrit : « Tu ne muselleras pas le bœuf qui foule [le grain]. »
fr.B: Car il est écrit dans la Loi de Moïse : « Ne mets pas de muselière au bœuf qui foule le grain. »
fr.R: La Loi de Moïse dit : « Quand un bœuf foule le grain, ne l’empêche pas de manger en lui fermant la bouche. »

decisions.choice: a quotation of Deuteronomy 25:4
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek translation of Deuteronomy 25:4. Paul quotes the same command, with "the worker deserves his wages", in 1 Timothy 5:18.

decisions.choice: threshing: oxen walked over cut grain on a threshing floor, or pulled a heavy board across it, to loosen the grain; a muzzle would stop the ox from eating as it worked
decisions.reason: The command lets the working animal eat from the grain it is threshing. Paul applies it to those who work for the gospel (verses 10-11).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: κημώσεις, a rare word for "muzzle"
alternatives: φιμώσεις, the more common word, used in the Greek Old Testament and in 1 Timothy 5:18
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the more common verb found in the Greek translation of Deuteronomy; the SBLGNT reads the rarer one, which scribes would be more likely to replace than to introduce. The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you shall not: a future tense used as a command
decisions.reason: The future with Οὐ is the form of the commandments in the Greek Old Testament ("you shall not").

decisions.choice: do not put a muzzle on its mouth (R)
decisions.reason: "Muzzle" as a verb is less familiar; Readable says what is done.

source.text: μὴ τῶν βοῶν μέλει τῷ θεῷ, ἢ δι’ ἡμᾶς πάντως λέγει;

records.literal_gloss: Not for the oxen is there care to the God, \v 10 or because of us certainly does he say [it]?

en.L: Is it for oxen that God is concerned, \v 10 or does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} certainly say [it] for our sake?
en.B: Is it oxen that God is concerned about here? \v 10 Or is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not surely speaking for our sake?
en.R: When God said this, was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} only thinking about oxen? \v 10 Surely {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking about us.

fr.L: Est-ce des bœufs que Dieu se soucie, \v 10 ou bien est-ce assurément à cause de nous qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [le] dit ?
fr.B: Est-ce des bœufs que Dieu se préoccupe ici ? \v 10 N’est-ce pas plutôt pour nous qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parle, sans aucun doute ?
fr.R: Quand Dieu a dit cela, pensait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} seulement aux bœufs ? \v 10 Bien sûr que non : c’est de nous qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait.

decisions.choice: God's concern in this command is not mainly for oxen but for people
alternatives: God does not care about animals at all
decisions.reason: μὴ expects the answer no. Paul does not deny that God cares for animals (Psalm 104:14-27; Matthew 6:26); he says that the purpose of this law reaches beyond oxen. Deuteronomy 25 is mostly about fair treatment of people, and Jewish teachers also drew lessons for people from laws about animals.

decisions.choice: certainly: without doubt
decisions.reason: πάντως can mean "altogether" or "surely, of course". "Altogether" would deny that the command was ever about oxen, which goes beyond m1; "certainly" fits the confident answer of verse 10.

decisions.choice: he says: God, speaking in Scripture
decisions.reason: The subject of λέγει is not named. The nearest subject is God in verse 9, and Paul treats the words of Scripture as God speaking.

decisions.choice: for our sake: for people, and especially those who work for the gospel
decisions.reason: The following verses apply the command to those who plow and thresh in hope, and then to Paul and his co-workers (verse 11).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to God (m3).

decisions.choice: only (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" so that the question is not heard as denying that God cares for animals (m1).

source.text: δι’ ἡμᾶς γὰρ ἐγράφη, ὅτι ὀφείλει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ὁ ἀροτριῶν ἀροτριᾶν, καὶ ὁ ἀλοῶν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τοῦ μετέχειν.

records.literal_gloss: For sake of us for it was written, that ought in hope the [one] plowing to plow, and the [one] threshing in hope of the sharing.

en.L: Yes, for our sake it was written, that the one plowing ought to plow in hope, and the one threshing [ought to thresh] in hope of sharing [in the crop].
en.B: Yes, this was written with us in mind: the one who plows ought to do so in hope, and the one who threshes ought to work expecting a share of the harvest.
en.R: Yes, it was written for us. The farmer who plows the field and the worker who threshes the grain should both be able to hope for part of the crop.

fr.L: Oui, c’est à cause de nous que cela a été écrit : celui qui laboure doit labourer dans l’espérance, et celui qui foule [le grain doit le faire] dans l’espérance d’avoir sa part [de la récolte].
fr.B: Oui, c’est en pensant à nous que cela a été écrit : celui qui laboure doit labourer avec espoir, et celui qui foule le grain doit travailler en espérant recevoir sa part de la récolte.
fr.R: Oui, cela a été écrit pour nous. Le paysan qui laboure son champ et l’ouvrier qui foule le grain doivent pouvoir espérer, tous les deux, une part de la récolte.

decisions.choice: yes: γὰρ confirms the answer to the question just asked
decisions.reason: After a question expecting "for our sake", γὰρ has the force of "yes indeed".

decisions.choice: that: ὅτι introduces what the command means for people, a principle drawn from it
alternatives: because: the reason it was written for us
the start of a quotation from some other writing
decisions.reason: ὅτι can introduce content ("that") or a reason ("because"). No known Scripture has these words, so they are probably Paul's statement of the principle in the command. Either way the meaning is that those who work should share in what their work produces.

decisions.choice: in hope: expecting a share of the crop the work produces
decisions.reason: Plowing and threshing begin and end the farmer's year. Each worker labors expecting to share in the harvest, as the ox eats while it threshes.

decisions.choice: [in the crop] (L); a share of the harvest (B); part of the crop (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the object of "sharing" understood; all levels name it.

source.text: εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν τὰ πνευματικὰ ἐσπείραμεν, μέγα εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῶν τὰ σαρκικὰ θερίσομεν;

records.literal_gloss: If we to you the spiritual [things] sowed, [is it] great if we of you the fleshly [things] will reap?

en.L: If we sowed the spiritual [things] for you, [is it] a great [thing] if we reap the fleshly [things] from you?
en.B: We sowed among you the things of the Spirit. Is it so much to ask, then, that we reap from you the things the body needs?
en.R: We planted God's message among you like seed in a field. Is it asking too much if we gather a harvest of food and other help from you?

fr.L: Si nous, nous avons semé pour vous les [biens] spirituels, [est-ce] une grande [chose] si nous, nous moissonnons vos [biens] charnels ?
fr.B: Nous avons semé parmi vous les biens de l’Esprit. Est-ce donc trop demander que nous récoltions de vous ce dont le corps a besoin ?
fr.R: Nous avons semé le message de Dieu parmi vous, comme on sème des graines dans un champ. Est-ce trop demander que nous récoltions chez vous de la nourriture et d’autres formes d’aide ?

decisions.choice: sowed ... reap: a farming picture for giving and receiving
decisions.reason: The picture carries on from verse 10. Paul's preaching was the sowing; support from the church would be a small harvest in return (compare Galatians 6:6; Romans 15:27).

decisions.choice: spiritual things: the gospel and the blessings that come by the Spirit
decisions.reason: πνευματικός means what belongs to the Spirit (2:13-15; 12:1).

decisions.choice: fleshly things: material needs such as food and shelter, with no moral sense
alternatives: things that belong to sinful human nature, as in 3:1, 3
decisions.reason: Set against "spiritual things", σαρκικὰ here means what belongs to bodily life, as in Romans 15:27. It does not carry the bad sense it has in 3:1-3.

decisions.choice: is it a great thing: is it too much to expect
decisions.reason: μέγα in a question asks whether something is a big matter; the expected answer is no.

decisions.choice: fleshly [things] (L); the things the body needs (B); food and other help (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "fleshly", the book's word for this family, so the link with 3:1-3 can be seen. Balanced and Readable say what the word means here (m3).

decisions.choice: charnels (L); ce dont le corps a besoin (B); de la nourriture et d'autres formes d'aide (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "charnels", the adjective of "la chair", so that the link with 3:1-3 can be seen, as the English keeps "fleshly". French "charnel" often suggests the body's desires or sin; here the word has no moral sense (m3), so Balanced and Readable say what is meant.

source.text: εἰ ἄλλοι τῆς ὑμῶν ἐξουσίας μετέχουσιν, οὐ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: If others of the over you right share, not more we?

en.L: If others share [in] the right over you, [do] not we more?
en.B: If others share in this right to your support, do we not have a greater claim to it?
en.R: Others have a right to be supported by you. Do we not have even more right than they do?

fr.L: Si d’autres ont part au droit sur vous, [n’est-ce] pas plutôt nous ?
fr.B: Si d’autres ont part à ce droit d’être soutenus par vous, n’y avons-nous pas encore plus droit ?
fr.R: D’autres ont le droit d’être soutenus par vous. N’avons-nous pas ce droit encore plus qu’eux ?

decisions.choice: the right over you: the right to receive support from you
alternatives: your own right, the right you have
decisions.reason: ὑμῶν is an objective genitive: a claim on the Corinthians. The argument of verses 4-11 is about the right to be supported by the church one serves.

decisions.choice: others: other teachers who had worked in Corinth and accepted support there
decisions.reason: Apollos had taught in Corinth (3:4-6), and Cephas may have visited (1:12). In 2 Corinthians 11:7-12, 20 Paul contrasts himself with teachers who took money from the church. Paul, who founded the church (4:15), would have the greater claim.

decisions.choice: a question that expects yes: we have it all the more
decisions.reason: οὐ μᾶλλον means "not more?", asking the readers to agree.

decisions.choice: this right to your support (B); a right to be supported by you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the right is (m1). "Right" is kept at every level for this word, as in 8:9.

source.text: Ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐχρησάμεθα τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ταύτῃ, ἀλλὰ πάντα στέγομεν ἵνα μή τινα ἐγκοπὴν δῶμεν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: But not we used the right this, but all things we bear so that not any hindrance we may give to the gospel of the Christ.

en.L: But we did not use this right; rather we bear all things, so that we may not put any hindrance [in the way] of the gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Yet we never claimed this right. We put up with every hardship so as not to block the path of the gospel of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in any way.
en.R: But we never used this right. We put up with all kinds of hardship so that nothing would hold back the good news about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Mais nous n’avons pas usé de ce droit ; au contraire, nous supportons tout, afin de ne causer aucun obstacle à l’Évangile du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Pourtant, nous n’avons jamais fait valoir ce droit. Nous supportons toutes les épreuves pour ne barrer d’aucune façon la route à l’Évangile du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Mais nous n’avons jamais utilisé ce droit. Nous supportons toutes sortes de difficultés pour que rien ne freine la bonne nouvelle du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

decisions.choice: bear: endure, put up with hardship
decisions.reason: στέγω means to bear up under something, as in 13:7 and 1 Thessalonians 3:1, 5. Paul means the hunger, tiredness and poverty of working for his own keep (4:11-12).

decisions.choice: hindrance: something that blocks a way and holds back progress
decisions.reason: ἐγκοπὴν comes from a word for cutting into a road to stop an advance. Taking money could make the gospel look like one more paid philosophy, or tie the preacher to a wealthy patron (compare 2 Corinthians 2:17; 1 Thessalonians 2:5-9).

decisions.choice: the gospel of Christ: the good news about Christ
decisions.reason: Christ is the content of the message (1:23; 15:3-5).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has the article, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: bear (L); put up with every hardship (B); put up with all kinds of hardship (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is borne (m1).

decisions.choice: l'Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the letters and Colossians does: Readable says "la bonne nouvelle" because "Évangile" is church language. The same holds in 9:14-23.

source.text: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ τὰ ἱερὰ ἐργαζόμενοι τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐσθίουσιν, οἱ τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ παρεδρεύοντες τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ συμμερίζονται;

records.literal_gloss: Not know you that those the sacred [things] working the [things] from the temple eat, those at the altar attending with the altar share?

en.L: Do you not know that those who work [at] the sacred [things] eat the [things] from the temple, [and] those who attend at the altar share with the altar?
en.B: Do you not know that those who carry out the temple's sacred work get their food from the temple, and those who wait on the altar receive a portion of what is offered on it?
en.R: Surely you know that people who work in the temple get their food from it. Those who serve at the altar get part of the sacrifices offered there.

fr.L: Ne savez-vous pas que ceux qui accomplissent les [services] sacrés mangent [ce qui vient] du temple, [et que] ceux qui se tiennent auprès de l’autel ont part avec l’autel ?
fr.B: Ne savez-vous pas que ceux qui accomplissent le service sacré du temple tirent leur nourriture du temple, et que ceux qui servent à l’autel reçoivent une part de ce qu’on y offre ?
fr.R: Vous le savez bien : ceux qui travaillent dans le temple y reçoivent leur nourriture. Ceux qui servent à l’autel reçoivent une part des sacrifices qu’on y offre.

decisions.choice: the priests and Levites of the temple in Jerusalem, who lived on parts of the offerings
decisions.reason: The Law of Moses gave the priests and Levites a share of the sacrifices and gifts in place of land (Numbers 18:8-31; Deuteronomy 18:1-5). Pagan priests in Corinth also ate from sacrifices, so the picture would be clear to every reader, but the language fits Israel's temple.

decisions.choice: share with the altar: receive part of the sacrifices offered on the altar
decisions.reason: Part of a sacrifice was burned on the altar and part went to the priests (Leviticus 7:6-10, 28-36), so the altar and the priest "shared" the offering.

decisions.choice: two clauses side by side with no "and": the second restates the first
decisions.reason: Greek leaves out the joining word; the two clauses make one point.

decisions.choice: receive a portion of what is offered on it (B); get part of the sacrifices offered there (R)
decisions.reason: "Share with the altar" is not natural English; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2).

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὁ κύριος διέταξεν τοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον καταγγέλλουσιν ἐκ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ζῆν.

records.literal_gloss: So also the Lord directed to those the gospel proclaiming from the gospel to live.

en.L: So also the Lord directed those who proclaim the gospel to live from the gospel.
en.B: In just this way the Lord directed that those who announce the gospel should live from the gospel.
en.R: In the same way, the Lord Jesus gave a command. Those who tell the good news should receive their living from that work.

fr.L: De même aussi, le Seigneur a ordonné à ceux qui annoncent l’Évangile de vivre de l’Évangile.
fr.B: Tout aussi bien, le Seigneur a prescrit que ceux qui annoncent l’Évangile vivent de l’Évangile.
fr.R: De la même façon, le Seigneur Jésus a donné un ordre : ceux qui annoncent la bonne nouvelle doivent recevoir de quoi vivre grâce à ce travail.

decisions.choice: the Lord's command: Jesus' instruction that those he sent out should be fed by those they served
decisions.reason: When Jesus sent out his disciples, he told them to take no money and to eat what they were given, "for the worker deserves his food" (Matthew 10:10) or "his wages" (Luke 10:7). Paul quotes the saying in 1 Timothy 5:18. As in 7:10, he cites a teaching of Jesus as a command.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: In Paul's letters κύριος without further description usually means Jesus, and the command matches Jesus' words in the Gospels (m1).

decisions.choice: live from the gospel: be supported by those to whom one preaches
decisions.reason: The gospel here stands for the work of preaching it and the community it creates.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, who gave the command (m2).

decisions.choice: receive their living from that work (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what living from the gospel means (m3). "Good news" is used once for the two mentions of the gospel.

source.text: Ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ κέχρημαι οὐδενὶ τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: I but not have used none of these.

en.L: But I have used none of these.
en.B: But I have not made use of any of these rights.
en.R: But I have not used even one of these rights.

fr.L: Mais moi, je n’ai usé de rien de tout cela.
fr.B: Mais moi, je n’ai fait valoir aucun de ces droits.
fr.R: Mais moi, je n’ai utilisé aucun de ces droits, pas un seul.

decisions.choice: I: Paul himself, set in contrast to the others; these: the rights argued for in verses 4-14
decisions.reason: The emphatic Ἐγὼ marks a turn from "we" to Paul's own case, which he explains in verses 15-18.

decisions.choice: rights (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "these" are (m1).

source.text: οὐκ ἔγραψα δὲ ταῦτα ἵνα οὕτως γένηται ἐν ἐμοί, καλὸν γάρ μοι μᾶλλον ἀποθανεῖν ἤ τὸ καύχημά μου οὐδεὶς κενώσει.

records.literal_gloss: Not I wrote but these things that thus it might be in me; good for to me rather to die than — the boasting of me no one will make empty.

en.L: And I have not written these things so that it may be done thus in my case; for [it would be] good for me rather to die than— no one will make my boasting empty!
en.B: I have not written this to have it done for me. I would rather die than that. No one will take away my reason to be proud!
en.R: I have not written this to ask you to start supporting me. I would rather die than let anyone take away the thing I am proud of.

fr.L: Et je n’ai pas écrit cela pour qu’il en soit ainsi à mon égard ; car [il serait] bon pour moi de mourir plutôt que… personne ne réduira à néant ce dont je me vante !
fr.B: Je n’ai pas écrit cela pour qu’on le fasse pour moi. J’aimerais mieux mourir que cela. Personne ne m’enlèvera ma raison d’être fier !
fr.R: Je n’ai pas écrit cela pour vous demander de commencer à me soutenir. J’aimerais mieux mourir que de laisser quelqu’un m’enlever ce dont je suis fier.

decisions.choice: a broken sentence: Paul begins "I would rather die than ..." and breaks off with "no one will empty my boast!"
alternatives: a smooth sentence: "than that anyone should make my boast empty"
decisions.reason: After ἤ the expected clause does not come; the sentence breaks off and starts again, as happens when someone speaks with strong feeling.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "no one will make my boast empty"
alternatives: "than that anyone should make my boast empty"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts smooth the broken sentence into a purpose clause. The SBLGNT, with early manuscripts, keeps the harder reading, which scribes were more likely to correct than to create. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: boast: the ground of Paul's pride, here his preaching without pay
decisions.reason: καύχημα is what one is proud of. Verse 18 shows what it is: offering the gospel free of charge. Paul's pride is not in himself but in serving without being a burden (2 Corinthians 11:9-10).

decisions.choice: make empty: take away, leave with nothing
decisions.reason: κενόω means to empty or make void (1:17). If he accepted pay, his reason for pride would be gone.

decisions.choice: boasting (L); reason to be proud (B); the thing I am proud of (R)
decisions.reason: By the book-wide rule, Literal says "boasting", and Balanced and Readable say "proud" where the argument does not turn on the word itself. Here Paul's "boast" is good pride in serving freely (m3), which "boast" in English would make sound bad.

decisions.choice: I would rather die than that. No one ... (B); I would rather die than let anyone take away ... (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced finishes the first clause with "than that" and keeps the outburst as a separate sentence. Readable joins the two into one plain sentence, which states the sense of the broken one (m1).

decisions.choice: to ask you to start supporting me (R)
alternatives: so that it may be done in my case
decisions.reason: Readable says what "it" is: the support he has refused.

decisions.choice: ce dont je me vante (L); ma raison d'être fier (B); ce dont je suis fier (R); the same in 9:16
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the "se vanter" family so that the boasting words can be traced through the letter, as in 5:6. "Ma vantardise" would make Paul's good pride in serving without pay (m3) sound bad, so Literal uses the verb, which can be said of good pride. Balanced and Readable follow the English "proud", by the book-wide rule.

source.text: ἐὰν γὰρ εὐαγγελίζωμαι, οὐκ ἔστιν μοι καύχημα, ἀνάγκη γάρ μοι ἐπίκειται· οὐαὶ γάρ μοί ἐστιν ἐὰν μὴ εὐαγγελίσωμαι.

records.literal_gloss: If for I preach the gospel, not is to me boasting, necessity for on me is laid; woe for to me is if not I preach the gospel.

en.L: For if I preach the gospel, there is no boasting for me, for necessity is laid on me; for woe is me if I do not preach the gospel.
en.B: Preaching the gospel gives me no reason to be proud, for I am under compulsion. It will go hard with me if I do not preach the gospel!
en.R: Telling the good news is not something I can be proud of. I have to do it, because God has given me no choice. How terrible it would be for me if I did not tell the good news!

fr.L: Car si j’annonce l’Évangile, il n’y a là pour moi [aucune raison de] me vanter, car une nécessité m’est imposée ; car malheur à moi si je n’annonce pas l’Évangile !
fr.B: Annoncer l’Évangile ne me donne aucune raison d’être fier, car c’est une obligation qui s’impose à moi. Malheur à moi si je n’annonce pas l’Évangile !
fr.R: Annoncer la bonne nouvelle, ce n’est pas quelque chose dont je peux être fier. Je dois le faire, parce que Dieu ne m’a pas laissé le choix. Ce serait terrible pour moi si je n’annonçais pas la bonne nouvelle !

decisions.choice: boasting: a reason for pride
decisions.reason: καύχημα is the same word as in verse 15. Preaching itself gives Paul no ground for pride, because he has no choice about it; what he can be proud of is preaching without pay (verse 18).

decisions.choice: necessity is laid on me: God's call compels Paul to preach
decisions.reason: Christ appeared to Paul and sent him to the nations (Acts 9:15; 26:16-18; Galatians 1:15-16). Like Jeremiah, he cannot keep silent (Jeremiah 20:9).

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of coming disaster, here God's judgment on an unfaithful servant
decisions.reason: οὐαὶ announces trouble, often from God (Matthew 23:13-29). Refusing his commission would bring Paul under judgment.

decisions.choice: boasting (L); reason to be proud (B); something I can be proud of (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 15, by the book-wide rule for this word.

decisions.choice: God has given me no choice (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the source of the compulsion (m2).

decisions.choice: woe is me (L); It will go hard with me (B); How terrible it would be for me (R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is old-fashioned; Balanced and Readable give the sense (m3).

decisions.choice: malheur à moi (L, B); Ce serait terrible pour moi (R)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "It will go hard with me" because "woe" is old-fashioned in English. French "malheur à" is still current and keeps the cry of coming judgment (m3), so Balanced keeps it, as the style guide does for "Woe to you". Readable gives the sense, as the English does.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἑκὼν τοῦτο πράσσω, μισθὸν ἔχω· εἰ δὲ ἄκων, οἰκονομίαν πεπίστευμαι.

records.literal_gloss: If for willingly this I do, a wage I have; if but unwillingly, a stewardship I have been entrusted with.

en.L: For if I do this willingly, I have a wage; but if unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship.
en.B: If I did this by my own choice, I would have a reward. But if it is not my choice, I have simply been entrusted with a household manager's task.
en.R: If I had chosen this work for myself, I could expect a reward. But it was not my choice. God has trusted me with a job to do, like a manager in charge of a household.

fr.L: Car si je fais cela de bon gré, j’ai un salaire ; mais si [c’est] malgré moi, c’est une intendance qui m’a été confiée.
fr.B: Si je le faisais de mon propre choix, j’aurais droit à une récompense. Mais si ce n’est pas mon choix, c’est simplement une charge d’intendant qui m’a été confiée.
fr.R: Si j’avais choisi ce travail moi-même, je pourrais attendre une récompense. Mais ce n’est pas moi qui l’ai choisi. Dieu m’a confié un travail à faire, comme à un intendant chargé de gérer une maison.

decisions.choice: the first condition is not Paul's case and the second is: he preaches under orders, as a steward
alternatives: both conditions are real possibilities, and Paul does preach willingly and has a reward
decisions.reason: Verse 16 says Paul has no choice about preaching, so "if unwillingly" describes his situation: not that he resents it, but that it was not his choice. He has no wage for doing his duty (Luke 17:7-10). Verse 18 then finds a different reward. Some read the first condition as Paul's own case too, taking "willingly" as his glad attitude.

decisions.choice: stewardship: the task of a household manager, often a slave, entrusted with the master's business
decisions.reason: οἰκονομία is the work of the household manager of 4:1-2, who answers to his master and is not paid for doing what he is told (compare Luke 12:42-48).

decisions.choice: wage: a reward earned by work done of one's own choice
decisions.reason: μισθός is pay or reward, as in 3:8, 14.

decisions.choice: wage, stewardship (L); reward, a household manager's task (B); reward, a manager in charge of a household (R)
decisions.reason: The book uses "wage" (Literal) and "reward" (Balanced, Readable) for this word, and "household manager" for the steward of 4:1-2.

decisions.choice: God has trusted me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who entrusted the task (m2).

decisions.choice: salaire (L), récompense (B, R); intendance (L), charge d'intendant (B), intendant chargé de gérer une maison (R)
decisions.reason: As the English "wage" and "reward". "Intendant" is the French word for the servant who manages a master's household (m2), the steward of 4:1-2; Readable says what his task is.

source.text: τίς οὖν μού ἐστιν ὁ μισθός;

records.literal_gloss: What then of me is the wage?

en.L: What then is my wage?
en.B: What, then, is my reward?
en.R: So what is my reward?

fr.L: Quel est donc mon salaire ?
fr.B: Quelle est donc ma récompense ?
fr.R: Alors, quelle est ma récompense ?

decisions.choice: the question leads to a paradox: Paul's reward is to take no pay
decisions.reason: Having said that he has no wage for preaching (verse 17), Paul asks what reward is left; the answer follows.

decisions.choice: wage (L); reward (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

source.text: ἵνα εὐαγγελιζόμενος ἀδάπανον θήσω τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, εἰς τὸ μὴ καταχρήσασθαι τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: That preaching the gospel free of charge I may make the gospel, so as not to make full use of the right of me in the gospel.

en.L: That in preaching the gospel I may make the gospel free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel.
en.B: It is this: when I preach the gospel, I offer it at no cost to anyone, and so I do not use to the full the right I have in the gospel.
en.R: My reward is this: I can tell the good news without asking anyone to pay. I do not insist on my right to be supported for telling the good news.

fr.L: [C’est] qu’en annonçant l’Évangile, je rends l’Évangile gratuit, de manière à ne pas user pleinement de mon droit dans l’Évangile.
fr.B: La voici : quand j’annonce l’Évangile, je l’offre sans qu’il en coûte rien à personne, et ainsi je n’use pas jusqu’au bout du droit que j’ai dans l’Évangile.
fr.R: Ma récompense, c’est de pouvoir annoncer la bonne nouvelle sans demander à personne de payer. Je n’exige pas mon droit d’être soutenu pour ce travail.

decisions.choice: that: ἵνα gives the content of the reward
alternatives: so that: the purpose of something left unstated
decisions.reason: The clause answers the question "What is my reward?": the reward is the freedom to offer the gospel free.

decisions.choice: free of charge: at no cost to those who hear
decisions.reason: ἀδάπανον means without expense. Paul supported himself so as not to be a burden (2 Corinthians 11:7-9; 2 Thessalonians 3:8).

decisions.choice: make full use of: use a right to its limit
decisions.reason: καταχράομαι can mean to use fully or to misuse (7:31). Paul has not called his right wrong (verses 4-14), so "use to the full" fits better.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the gospel"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "of Christ" after the first mention of the gospel. The earlier manuscripts lack it, and the SBLGNT follows them. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: right (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: "Right" is kept for this word at every level, as in 8:9 and 9:4-12. Readable says which right: to be supported.

source.text: Ἐλεύθερος γὰρ ὢν ἐκ πάντων πᾶσιν ἐμαυτὸν ἐδούλωσα, ἵνα τοὺς πλείονας κερδήσω·

records.literal_gloss: Free for being from all, to all myself I enslaved, so that the more I might gain;

en.L: For being free from all [people], I enslaved myself to all, so that I might gain the more.
en.B: No one has any claim on me, yet I have become everyone's slave, so as to win over a greater number.
en.R: No one owns me. I am free. But I have made myself a slave to everyone, so that I can win more people to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Car, étant libre à l’égard de tous, je me suis rendu esclave de tous, afin de gagner le plus grand nombre.
fr.B: Personne n’a de droit sur moi, et pourtant je suis devenu l’esclave de tout le monde, pour en gagner un plus grand nombre.
fr.R: Personne n’est mon maître. Je suis libre. Mais je me suis fait l’esclave de tout le monde, pour gagner plus de gens au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

decisions.choice: free from all: free from every person, under no one's authority
decisions.reason: πάντων is masculine, and is set against πᾶσιν, "to all" people: no one owns Paul, but he serves everyone.

decisions.choice: enslaved myself: put himself in the position of a slave, giving up his rights to serve others
decisions.reason: δουλόω is the verb of δοῦλος (slave). Paul freely takes the place of a slave, as Christ did (Philippians 2:7), and as he asked the strong to do for the weak (8:13).

decisions.choice: gain: win people for Christ
decisions.reason: κερδαίνω is a business word for making a profit (Philippians 3:7-8). Here, and in verses 20-22, it means winning people to faith (compare Matthew 18:15; 1 Peter 3:1).

decisions.choice: the more: as many as possible, more than he would win otherwise
decisions.reason: With the article, πλείονας means "the more", that is, a greater number than if he insisted on his rights.

decisions.choice: enslaved myself (L); everyone's slave (B); a slave to everyone (R)
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free: Paul, free from all, makes himself everyone's slave (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: win ... to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul wins people to (m3). "Win" is used at Balanced and Readable for this verb in verses 19-22.

decisions.choice: gagner at every level (9:19-22)
decisions.reason: The English has "gain" at Literal and "win" at Balanced and Readable. French "gagner" says both, and "gagner quelqu'un" is the usual French for winning a person over (m3), so one verb serves every level.

source.text: καὶ ἐγενόμην τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὡς Ἰουδαῖος, ἵνα Ἰουδαίους κερδήσω· τοῖς ὑπὸ νόμον ὡς ὑπὸ νόμον, μὴ ὢν αὐτὸς ὑπὸ νόμον, ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον κερδήσω·

records.literal_gloss: And I became to the Jews as a Jew, so that Jews I might gain; to those under law as under law, not being myself under law, so that those under law I might gain;

en.L: And to the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might gain Jews; to those under [the] law [I became] as under [the] law, though not being myself under [the] law, so that I might gain those under [the] law.
en.B: And so to the Jews I became as a Jew, to win Jews over. For the sake of those under the law I became as one under the law, though I am not myself under the law, to win over those under the law.
en.R: When I was with Jewish people, I lived like a Jew, so that I could win them. When I was with people who live under the law of Moses, I lived as if I were under that law, so that I could win them. But I am not under the law myself.

fr.L: Et je suis devenu pour les Juifs comme un Juif, afin de gagner des Juifs ; pour ceux [qui sont] sous la Loi, comme [si j’étais] sous la Loi, bien que je ne sois pas moi-même sous la Loi, afin de gagner ceux [qui sont] sous la Loi.
fr.B: Ainsi, avec les Juifs, je suis devenu comme un Juif, pour gagner des Juifs. Pour ceux qui sont sous la Loi, je suis devenu comme quelqu’un qui est sous la Loi, bien que je ne sois pas moi-même sous la Loi, pour gagner ceux qui sont sous la Loi.
fr.R: Quand j’étais avec des Juifs, j’ai vécu comme un Juif, pour pouvoir les gagner. Quand j’étais avec des gens qui vivent sous la Loi de Moïse, j’ai vécu comme si j’étais sous cette Loi, pour pouvoir les gagner. Pourtant, je ne suis pas moi-même sous la Loi.

decisions.choice: as a Jew: Paul kept Jewish customs, such as food laws and festivals, when he was among Jews
alternatives: he pretended to be a Jew
decisions.reason: Paul was a Jew by birth (2 Corinthians 11:22; Philippians 3:5), but he no longer based his standing with God on keeping the law. Among Jews he still kept their customs so as not to put obstacles in their way (Acts 16:3; 21:20-26).

decisions.choice: under the law: living under the Law of Moses as the rule that governs one's life before God
decisions.reason: Paul uses the phrase for life under the authority of the law of Moses (Romans 6:14-15; Galatians 4:4-5, 21). Those under the law are Jews, and perhaps also Gentiles who had taken on the law. Paul says he is not under the law in this sense, though he is not lawless either (verse 21).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: include "though not being myself under the law"
decisions.reason: The phrase is in the early manuscripts but missing from many later ones, perhaps because a scribe's eye skipped from one "under the law" to the next, or because the statement seemed too strong. The SBLGNT includes it. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: as: like, taking the position of
decisions.reason: ὡς marks that Paul took on their way of life for a purpose. He does the same in each pair (verses 20-21), but not in verse 22.

decisions.choice: became as ... gain (L); became as ... win over (B); lived like ... win (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "becoming as a Jew" meant in practice (m1). "Win" is used for this verb at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 19.

source.text: τοῖς ἀνόμοις ὡς ἄνομος, μὴ ὢν ἄνομος θεοῦ ἀλλ’ ἔννομος Χριστοῦ, ἵνα κερδάνω τοὺς ἀνόμους·

records.literal_gloss: To the without-law [ones] as without law, not being without law of God but within law of Christ, so that I might gain the without-law [ones];

en.L: To those without law [I became] as without law, not being without [the] law of God but within [the] law of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, so that I might gain those without law.
en.B: To those without the law I became as one without the law, to win over those without the law. Yet I am not without God's law; I live within the law of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: When I was with people who do not have the law of Moses, I lived as they do, so that I could win them. But that does not mean I ignore God's law. I obey the law of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Pour ceux [qui sont] sans loi, [je suis devenu] comme sans loi, n’étant pas sans loi [à l’égard] de Dieu, mais dans la loi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, afin de gagner ceux [qui sont] sans loi.
fr.B: Pour ceux qui sont sans la Loi, je suis devenu comme quelqu’un qui est sans la Loi, pour gagner ceux qui sont sans la Loi. Pourtant, je ne suis pas sans loi à l’égard de Dieu : je vis dans la loi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Quand j’étais avec des gens qui n’ont pas la Loi de Moïse, j’ai vécu comme eux, pour pouvoir les gagner. Mais cela ne veut pas dire que je ne tiens pas compte de la loi de Dieu. J’obéis à la loi du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

decisions.choice: those without law: Gentiles, who do not live by the Law of Moses
decisions.reason: ἄνομος can mean "wicked", but here it is set against "those under the law" and means Gentiles, who do not have Moses' law (Romans 2:12, 14). Paul ate with them and did not ask them to keep Jewish customs (Galatians 2:11-14).

decisions.choice: not without the law of God but within the law of Christ: Paul is not free of obligation to God; he is bound to Christ's law
alternatives: not lawless toward God but law-abiding toward Christ, as two separate relations
decisions.reason: ἄνομος θεοῦ and ἔννομος Χριστοῦ are genitives of relation: Paul does not stand outside God's law; he stands within the law that belongs to Christ. Being free from the law of Moses does not mean being free from God's will.

decisions.choice: the law of Christ: God's will as Christ taught it and lived it, summed up in love
alternatives: the Law of Moses as Christ interpreted it
decisions.reason: Paul uses the phrase in Galatians 6:2, where bearing one another's burdens fulfils the law of Christ; love fulfils the law (Romans 13:8-10; Galatians 5:14; John 13:34).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the genitives θεοῦ and Χριστοῦ
alternatives: the datives θεῷ and Χριστῷ ("without law to God, within law to Christ")
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have dative forms. The sense hardly changes. The SBLGNT follows the earlier manuscripts. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: within [the] law (L); live within the law (B); obey the law (R)
decisions.reason: ἔννομος means "in the law", one who lives inside it. "Under" is kept for the law of Moses in verse 20, so the contrast stays clear.

decisions.choice: the purpose clause moved before the qualification (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "to win over those without the law" with the clause it belongs to, and gives the qualification its own sentence, so the long sentence stays clear.

source.text: ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν ἀσθενής, ἵνα τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς κερδήσω· τοῖς πᾶσιν γέγονα πάντα, ἵνα πάντως τινὰς σώσω.

records.literal_gloss: I became to the weak weak, so that the weak I might gain; to the all I have become all [things], so that by all means some I might save.

en.L: To the weak I became weak, so that I might gain the weak; I have become all things to {{gender:all [people]|all [men]}}, so that by all means I might save some.
en.B: With the weak I became weak, to win over the weak. To {{gender:all people|all men}} I have become all things, so that one way or another I may save some.
en.R: With people who are weak, I became weak too, so that I could win them. I have become all things to {{gender:all people|all men}}. In whatever way I can, I want to save some of them.

fr.L: Je suis devenu faible pour les faibles, afin de gagner les faibles ; pour tous je suis devenu tout, afin d’en sauver de toute manière quelques-uns.
fr.B: Avec les faibles, je suis devenu faible, pour gagner les faibles. Je suis devenu tout pour tout le monde, afin d’en sauver quelques-uns, d’une manière ou d’une autre.
fr.R: Avec les gens qui sont faibles, je suis devenu faible moi aussi, pour pouvoir les gagner. Je suis devenu tout pour tout le monde. De toutes les façons possibles, je veux en sauver quelques-uns.

decisions.choice: the weak: probably believers with a weak conscience, as in chapter 8
alternatives: people who are weak in social standing or power
unbelievers who are weak in a general sense
decisions.reason: ἀσθενής is the word for the weak in 8:7-12, and Paul has just offered himself as an example of giving up rights for them (8:13). But "win" elsewhere in these verses means winning people to faith, so some take the weak as unbelievers, or as the poor and powerless (1:27).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "I became weak", without "as"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "as" to match verses 20-21. The SBLGNT, with early manuscripts, lacks it: with the weak, Paul does not only act like them; he shares their weakness (2 Corinthians 11:29). Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: all things to all people: Paul adapts his way of life to every kind of person
alternatives: he changes his message to suit his hearers
decisions.reason: The summary covers the examples of verses 20-22. Paul changes how he lives, not the gospel, which he will not alter (15:1-3; Galatians 1:8).

decisions.choice: by all means save some: by every way possible, bring at least some to salvation
decisions.reason: πάντως means "in every way" or "at any rate". God saves; Paul calls himself the means, as in 7:16 and Romans 11:14.

decisions.choice: {{gender:all [people]|all [men]}} (L); {{gender:all people|all men}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: πᾶσιν means all people, men and women.

decisions.choice: by all means (L); one way or another (B); in any way I can (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the adverb in everyday words.

decisions.choice: "tous" (L), "tout le monde" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:all people|all men}} because "all men" is the traditional form. French "tous" and "tout le monde" already mean all people, men and women (m3), and adding a noun only to carry the setting would weigh down Paul's short saying.

source.text: πάντα δὲ ποιῶ διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, ἵνα συγκοινωνὸς αὐτοῦ γένωμαι.

records.literal_gloss: All things but I do because of the gospel, so that a co-sharer of it I may become.

en.L: And I do all things because of the gospel, so that I may become a fellow sharer in it.
en.B: Everything I do is for the gospel's sake, so that I may have my share in it together with them.
en.R: I do all this because of the good news, so that I can share with others in what the good news brings.

fr.L: Et je fais tout à cause de l’Évangile, afin d’y avoir part avec [d’autres].
fr.B: Tout ce que je fais, je le fais pour l’Évangile, afin d’y avoir ma part avec eux.
fr.R: Je fais tout cela à cause de la bonne nouvelle, pour avoir part, avec les autres, à tout ce qu’elle apporte.

decisions.choice: a fellow sharer in it: one who shares in the blessings of the gospel together with those he wins
alternatives: a partner in the work of spreading the gospel
decisions.reason: συγκοινωνὸς means one who shares something with others. Paul does not assume that his own share in salvation is automatic; he wants to share in it with those he has won, which leads into the warning of verses 24-27. Some take it to mean that he wants to be a partner in the gospel's work.

decisions.choice: all things: everything he has described in verses 19-22
decisions.reason: πάντα sums up his becoming all things to all people.

decisions.choice: together with them (B); with others in what the good news brings (R)
decisions.reason: The prefix of συγκοινωνὸς means "together with"; Balanced and Readable name the others (m1).

source.text: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἐν σταδίῳ τρέχοντες πάντες μὲν τρέχουσιν, εἷς δὲ λαμβάνει τὸ βραβεῖον;

records.literal_gloss: Not know you that those in a stadium running all indeed run, one but receives the prize?

en.L: Do you not know that those running in a stadium all run, but one receives the prize?
en.B: Do you not know that every runner in the stadium races, yet only one is given the prize?
en.R: Do you not know that many runners race in the stadium, but only one of them wins the prize?

fr.L: Ne savez-vous pas que ceux qui courent dans le stade courent tous, mais qu’un seul reçoit le prix ?
fr.B: Ne savez-vous pas que, dans le stade, tous les coureurs prennent part à la course, mais qu’un seul se voit remettre le prix ?
fr.R: Ne savez-vous pas que beaucoup de coureurs font la course dans le stade, mais qu’un seul d’entre eux gagne le prix ?

decisions.choice: the stadium: the running track of the Greek games; Corinth hosted the Isthmian Games
decisions.reason: στάδιον was a race course of about 600 feet (180 meters), and the length of the race run on it. The Isthmian Games, held every two years near Corinth, were among the four great festivals of Greek athletics, so the Corinthians knew the scene well.

decisions.choice: the prize: the award given to the winner of a contest
decisions.reason: βραβεῖον is the victor's prize (Philippians 3:14). Verse 25 says what it was: a wreath.

decisions.choice: only one wins: the point is the effort of the winner, not that only one believer will be saved
decisions.reason: The picture is used for one lesson: run as the winner runs (verse 24b). Believers do not compete against one another.

decisions.choice: receives (L); is given (B); wins (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for receiving a prize.

source.text: οὕτως τρέχετε ἵνα καταλάβητε.

records.literal_gloss: Thus run so that you may obtain [it].

en.L: Run thus, so that you may obtain [it].
en.B: Run like that one, so as to win it.
en.R: So run your race to win the prize.

fr.L: Courez ainsi, afin de [le] remporter.
fr.B: Courez comme lui, de manière à le remporter.
fr.R: Alors courez votre course pour gagner le prix.

decisions.choice: run: a command; thus: in the way the winner runs
alternatives: a statement: "you run in this way"
decisions.reason: τρέχετε could be a statement or a command, but the exhortation of verses 24-27 shows it is a command. οὕτως points back to the one who wins.

decisions.choice: obtain: take hold of the prize, win it
decisions.reason: καταλαμβάνω is used in Philippians 3:12-14 of pressing on to take hold of the prize.

decisions.choice: like that one ... it (B); your race ... the prize (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose running is the model and what is won (m1).

source.text: πᾶς δὲ ὁ ἀγωνιζόμενος πάντα ἐγκρατεύεται, ἐκεῖνοι μὲν οὖν ἵνα φθαρτὸν στέφανον λάβωσιν, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄφθαρτον.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone but the [one] competing in all things exercises self-control, those indeed then so that a perishable wreath they may receive, we but an imperishable.

en.L: Now everyone who competes exercises self-control in all things; they then [do it] so that they may receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable [one].
en.B: Every competitor holds back from many things in training. They accept this to win a wreath that soon withers; we, to win one that never decays.
en.R: Athletes who compete in the games train hard and say no to many things. All that effort is for a crown of leaves that soon dries up. But we are running for a crown that will last forever.

fr.L: Or tout compétiteur se maîtrise en toutes choses ; eux [le font] donc pour recevoir une couronne périssable, mais nous, une impérissable.
fr.B: Tout athlète en compétition se prive de bien des choses à l’entraînement. Eux acceptent cela pour gagner une couronne de feuillage qui se fane vite ; nous, pour en gagner une qui ne s’abîmera jamais.
fr.R: Les athlètes qui participent aux jeux s’entraînent dur et disent non à beaucoup de choses. Tout cet effort, c’est pour une couronne de feuilles qui sèche vite. Mais nous, nous courons pour une couronne qui durera toujours.

decisions.choice: competes ... exercises self-control in all things: an athlete in the games keeps strict discipline in diet, rest and conduct
decisions.reason: ἀγωνίζομαι is the general word for competing in the games; ἐγκρατεύεται means to master oneself and go without things. Athletes in the Greek games trained for months beforehand under strict rules.

decisions.choice: a perishable wreath: the winner's wreath of leaves, which soon withered
decisions.reason: στέφανος here is a victor's wreath, not a king's crown. At the Isthmian Games it was made of pine, or of wild celery, which dried up within days.

decisions.choice: an imperishable wreath: the reward that lasts forever, given at Christ's coming
decisions.reason: The New Testament speaks of a crown of righteousness, life or glory given at the end (2 Timothy 4:8; James 1:12; 1 Peter 5:4). Paul uses ἄφθαρτος for the resurrection body in 15:52-54.

decisions.choice: wreath (L, B); crown of leaves (R)
decisions.reason: "Crown" suggests a king's gold crown; Literal and Balanced say "wreath", and Readable says "crown of leaves" so the contrast with a crown that lasts is plain (m2).

decisions.choice: holds back from many things (B); say no to many things (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what self-control meant for an athlete (m1).

decisions.choice: une couronne (L); une couronne de feuillage (B); une couronne de feuilles (R)
decisions.reason: French "couronne" is also the word for a victor's wreath, so Literal can keep it alone. Balanced and Readable add what it was made of, as the English "wreath" and "crown of leaves" do, so that the contrast with a crown that lasts is plain (m2). "Laurier" would name the wrong plant: the wreath of the Isthmian Games was of pine or wild celery.

source.text: ἐγὼ τοίνυν οὕτως τρέχω ὡς οὐκ ἀδήλως, οὕτως πυκτεύω ὡς οὐκ ἀέρα δέρων·

records.literal_gloss: I therefore thus run as not uncertainly, thus I box as not air beating;

en.L: I therefore run thus, as not uncertainly; I box thus, as not beating [the] air.
en.B: That is how I run: not like a runner unsure of the finish. That is how I box: not like a fighter swinging at empty air.
en.R: So I run with the finish line clearly in view. And I am a boxer whose punches land, not one who just punches the air.

fr.L: Moi donc, je cours ainsi, non pas à l’aveuglette ; je boxe ainsi, non comme battant l’air.
fr.B: Voilà comment je cours : pas comme un coureur qui ne sait pas où est l’arrivée. Voilà comment je boxe : pas comme un boxeur qui frappe dans le vide.
fr.R: Alors je cours en gardant bien en vue la ligne d’arrivée. Et je suis un boxeur dont les coups touchent, pas un boxeur qui frappe seulement dans le vide.

decisions.choice: not uncertainly: with a clear goal, not without aim
decisions.reason: ἀδήλως means without clear direction. A runner who does not know where the finish line is will not win.

decisions.choice: box ... beating the air: boxing was one of the contests of the games; a boxer who beats the air either shadow-boxes or misses his opponent
decisions.reason: πυκτεύω is the boxer's verb. Paul's effort is aimed at a real goal, not wasted motion.

decisions.choice: I therefore: Paul again offers himself as the example
decisions.reason: τοίνυν draws the conclusion from verse 25; Paul speaks of himself as in 8:13 and 9:15-23.

decisions.choice: unsure of the finish ... swinging at empty air (B); finish line clearly in view ... whose punches land (R)
alternatives: not uncertainly ... not beating the air
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the pictures (m1, m2). Readable states them positively.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ὑπωπιάζω μου τὸ σῶμα καὶ δουλαγωγῶ, μή πως ἄλλοις κηρύξας αὐτὸς ἀδόκιμος γένωμαι.

records.literal_gloss: But I strike under the eye of me the body and lead [it] as a slave, lest somehow to others having preached, myself disqualified I might become.

en.L: But I strike my body under the eye and lead [it] as a slave, lest somehow, having preached to others, I myself become disqualified.
en.B: Rather, I punish my body with blows and treat it as my servant, so that after preaching to others I will not myself be found disqualified.
en.R: I train my body hard and make it obey me, as a master makes a servant obey. I have preached God's message to others, and I do not want to end up disqualified myself.

fr.L: Mais je frappe mon corps sous l’œil et [le] mène en esclave, de peur qu’après avoir prêché aux autres, je ne sois moi-même disqualifié.
fr.B: Au contraire, je frappe durement mon corps et je le traite comme mon serviteur, pour ne pas être moi-même disqualifié après avoir prêché aux autres.
fr.R: J’entraîne durement mon corps et je l’oblige à m’obéir, comme un maître se fait obéir de son serviteur. J’ai prêché le message de Dieu aux autres, et je ne veux pas finir moi-même disqualifié.

decisions.choice: strike under the eye: a boxer's word, used for treating one's body with severe discipline
alternatives: punishing the body for its own sake
decisions.reason: ὑπωπιάζω means to hit someone in the face, to give a black eye, and so to treat harshly. Paul continues the boxing picture: his own body is the opponent he masters. He means discipline that serves the race, not self-punishment as a goal (compare Colossians 2:23).

decisions.choice: lead as a slave: make the body serve him, not rule him
decisions.reason: δουλαγωγέω means to lead off as a captive or to make someone a slave. The body, with its appetites, is to be the servant, as in 6:12-13, 19-20.

decisions.choice: disqualified: failing the test, and so not receiving the prize
alternatives: losing only a reward for service, while remaining saved
decisions.reason: ἀδόκιμος means tested and found not genuine (2 Corinthians 13:5-7). In the picture, an athlete who broke the rules was disqualified from the prize. Whether Paul means losing the imperishable wreath of verse 25, that is, final salvation, or losing approval for his ministry is debated. Chapter 10 goes on to warn that Israel received God's gifts and still fell.

decisions.choice: having preached: proclaimed the gospel
alternatives: having acted as herald at the games
decisions.reason: κηρύσσω is Paul's usual word for preaching (1:23; 15:11). At the games a herald announced the contests and the winners, and some hear that picture here too.

decisions.choice: strike under the eye, lead [it] as a slave (L); punish my body with blows, treat it as my servant (B); train my body hard, as a master makes a servant obey (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the force of the boxing word; Readable gives its sense in plain words (m1). "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m2) keeps the picture of the body made to serve, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: God's message (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul preached (m4).
